question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Speaking disrespectfully about sacred or religious things.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Blasphemy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Blasphemy means speaking disrespectfully or irreverently about God, sacred things, or religious beliefs. (ईश्वर या धार्मिक चीज़ों का अनादर करना)
◦ Example: The priest was shocked at what he considered blasphemy against the sacred texts.

• The word comes from the Greek word blasphemia, meaning "evil speaking" or "slander".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Mystic (रहस्यवादी): A person who seeks spiritual truth through meditation and contemplation rather than through reason; someone believing in mystical, spiritual experience.

• Option 3: Atheist (नास्तिक): A person who does not believe in the existence of God or any deity.

• Option 4: Theist (आस्तिक): A person who believes in the existence of God or gods.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes often tested by SSC: Agnostic (one who believes the existence of God cannot be known), Heretic (one who holds an opinion contrary to accepted religious doctrine), and Sacrilege (violation of something sacred).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined word segment in the given sentence.
Sanat has just arrived in Mysore on transfer; he requests his friend Raghu to help him find an appropriate location.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. a rented accommodation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sanat has "just arrived...on transfer", so the most logical thing his friend would help him find is a place to live — that is, rented accommodation (a house/flat to stay in).

• The original phrase "an appropriate location" is vague; the sentence context (a transfer to a new city) makes clear that Sanat needs a place to stay, not merely a "location". Option 2 correctly and precisely conveys this meaning without changing the sense of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "an allocation recommendation" is incorrect because it changes the meaning entirely — Sanat needs a place to live, not a recommendation for an allocation (which suggests an official assignment, not a search for housing).

• Option 3: "a proper junction" is incorrect because a "junction" refers to a place where roads/routes meet; it makes no sense in the context of someone newly transferred looking for a place to stay.

• Option 4: "a suitable elevation" is incorrect because "elevation" refers to height or altitude (or the front view of a building), which is irrelevant to the context of finding a place to live.

NOTE

• In sentence-improvement/substitution questions, always check that the replacement (i) fits the grammatical structure of the sentence and (ii) preserves or clarifies the intended meaning without introducing new, unrelated ideas.

• Commonly confused pair: "accommodation" (a place to live/stay) vs "accommodation" in the sense of "adjustment/compromise" — context decides which sense is meant.

question:
The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error.
Two of the world's / best forwards / has played alongside / David Beckham.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. has played alongside.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "Two of the world's best forwards", which is a plural subject (the head word is "forwards", and it is further confirmed by the number "Two").

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement: A plural subject must always take a plural verb. Since the subject here is plural, the verb must be "have played", not "has played".

• The segment "has played alongside" wrongly uses the singular auxiliary verb "has" with a plural subject, making it grammatically incorrect. It should read "have played alongside".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Two of the world's" is correct; it correctly forms the possessive plural phrase that introduces the subject.

• Option 2: "David Beckham." is correct; it is simply the object of the preposition "alongside" and needs no change.

• Option 3: "best forwards" is correct; "forwards" is correctly used in the plural to match "Two".

NOTE

• Watch for "One of the + plural noun" constructions — these take a singular verb (e.g., "One of the boys is absent"), whereas "Two/Some/Many of the + plural noun" take a plural verb (e.g., "Two of the boys are absent"). Do not confuse the two patterns.

• Other common subject-verb agreement traps tested by SSC: collective nouns (team, family, committee), indefinite pronouns (each, everyone, neither), and phrases joined by "along with", "as well as", "together with" (which do not make the subject plural).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Adequate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Sufficient.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Adequate means satisfactory or sufficient in quality or quantity for a particular purpose or need. (पर्याप्त)
◦ Example: The salary he earns is adequate for his family's needs.

• Sufficient carries the same core meaning — enough for a particular purpose — making it the closest synonym of "Adequate".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Evaluate (मूल्यांकन करना): To assess or judge the value, quality or importance of something. It is unrelated in meaning to "Adequate".

• Option 2: Hidden (छिपा हुआ): Kept out of sight or not easily seen; the opposite in sense — it has nothing to do with sufficiency.

• Option 4: Reconcile (मेल-मिलाप करना): To restore friendly relations between people, or to make two apparently conflicting things compatible.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Adequate" often asked in SSC: Ample, Enough, Satisfactory, Competent (in the sense of "adequately qualified").

• Do not confuse "Adequate" with "Adept" (skilled) — the two look similar but mean different things.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Brittle
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Fragile.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Brittle means hard but liable to break or snap easily; fragile. (भंगुर / आसानी से टूटने वाला)
◦ Example: Old, dry leaves become brittle and crumble at the slightest touch.

• Fragile means easily broken or damaged, which matches the meaning of "Brittle" exactly, making it the correct synonym.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Furtive (चोरी-छिपे किया गया): Done secretively or stealthily, to avoid being noticed — unrelated to physical breakability.

• Option 2: Fickle (चंचल/अस्थिर): Changing frequently, especially in loyalty or affection; not constant. It describes a person's nature, not a physical property.

• Option 4: Fatal (घातक): Causing death; deadly. It is unrelated to the meaning of "Brittle".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Brittle" tested by SSC: Crisp, Breakable, Delicate, Frail.

• Do not confuse "Fragile" with "Flexible" (able to bend without breaking) — the two are near-opposites in meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Cherish
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Nurture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Cherish means to protect and care for someone/something lovingly, or to hold a feeling or idea dearly in one's mind. (पोषण करना / प्रिय मानना)
◦ Example: She will always cherish the memories of her childhood.

• Nurture means to care for and encourage the growth or development of someone/something, which closely matches the caring, protective sense of "Cherish".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Neglect (उपेक्षा करना): To fail to care for or give attention to; the opposite of "Cherish".

• Option 2: Breach (उल्लंघन करना): To break or violate a rule, law or agreement; unrelated in meaning.

• Option 4: Afflict (पीड़ित करना): To cause pain or suffering to someone; again broadly opposite to the caring sense of "Cherish".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Cherish" tested by SSC: Treasure, Cling to, Foster, Prize, Value.

• Antonym pairing to remember: Cherish ↔ Neglect/Abandon/Disregard.

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
(O) attitude is
(P) or tendency in individuals
(Q) a broad-based behaviour
(R) which implies
(S) a hypothetical postulate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. OSRQP.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence must begin with the subject "attitude is" (O), since it is the only part that can logically start the sentence (it introduces the subject "attitude" with the verb "is").

• After the subject and verb, the complement should follow: "a hypothetical postulate" (S), giving "Attitude is a hypothetical postulate...".

• This is followed by the relative clause "which implies" (R), which needs an antecedent to attach to and leads into what the postulate implies.

• The clause then needs an object: "a broad-based behaviour" (Q), followed by its coordinated alternative, "or tendency in individuals" (P), which completes the sentence.

• Reading the full sentence: "Attitude is a hypothetical postulate which implies a broad-based behaviour or tendency in individuals." This is grammatically correct and makes complete logical sense.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. OSRQP.

Additional Information

• Option 1: SQPRO is incorrect because it begins with "a hypothetical postulate", which cannot start the sentence as it has no subject or verb preceding it.

• Option 3: OPQRS is incorrect because it places "or tendency in individuals (P)" immediately after "attitude is (O)", which is grammatically disconnected and meaningless.

• Option 4: OPSRQ is incorrect because it similarly places "P" right after "O", breaking the logical link between the subject and its complement.

NOTE

• In para/sentence jumble questions, always identify the part that can grammatically function as the opening (usually containing the subject and main verb) before looking for logical connectors like "which", "or", "and" to link the remaining parts.

• Watch for relative pronouns ("which", "who", "that") — they typically follow the noun/clause they modify and introduce the next logical unit of the sentence.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Material
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Abstract.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Material (as an adjective) means relating to physical objects or matter, rather than to the mind, spirit, or emotions; concrete/tangible. (भौतिक / वास्तविक)
◦ Example: Material possessions do not guarantee happiness.

• Abstract means existing in thought or as an idea, but not having a physical or concrete existence, which is the direct opposite of "Material", making it the correct antonym.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Cheap (सस्ता): Low in price or cost; it describes value/price, not the material-versus-non-physical distinction, so it is not an antonym of "Material".

• Option 3: Concrete (ठोस): Existing in a physical or material form — this is actually a synonym of "Material", not its opposite.

• Option 4: Temporary (अस्थायी): Lasting for a limited time only; it relates to duration, not to the physical-versus-abstract distinction.

NOTE

• Other antonym pairs frequently tested by SSC involving "Material": Material ↔ Spiritual / Immaterial / Abstract.

• Do not confuse "Material" (adjective, tangible) with "immaterial" (adjective, unimportant/irrelevant) — although they look like opposites by prefix, "immaterial" in common usage more often means "unimportant" rather than strictly "non-physical".

question:
Select the most appropriate homonyms from the given alternatives to fill in the blanks.
The rowing instructor commanded them to ________ in a ________.
A. row (verb)
B. roe
C. row (sequence)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. A, C.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first blank needs a verb describing what a rowing instructor commands people to do: "row" (verb) — meaning to propel a boat using oars. This is option A.

• The second blank follows "in a ___", describing the formation in which they should row: "row" (sequence) — meaning a number of people or things arranged in a straight line. This is option C.

• Rule — Homonyms: Homonyms are words that are spelled identically (and usually pronounced alike) but have different, unrelated meanings. Here, "row" (to paddle a boat) and "row" (a line/sequence) are spelled and pronounced identically but mean different things, making them true homonyms.

• Complete sentence: "The rowing instructor commanded them to row (paddle) in a row (straight line/formation)." This makes perfect contextual sense for a rowing class.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. A, C.

Additional Information

• Option 1: C, A is incorrect because it reverses the required order — the first blank (after "commanded them to") needs the verb "row" (A), not the noun "row" (C).

• Option 2: B, C is incorrect because "roe" (B, meaning fish eggs) cannot fit the first blank, which requires a verb describing an action the rowers perform.

• Option 3: A, B is incorrect because "roe" (fish eggs) makes no sense in the phrase "in a roe" — the second blank requires "row" (formation), not "roe".

NOTE

• Do not confuse homonyms (same spelling and pronunciation, different meaning, e.g., "row"/"row") with homophones (same pronunciation, different spelling and meaning, e.g., "roe"/"row"/"rho").

• "Roe" specifically refers to the mass of eggs found in a female fish.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
At a low ebb
option_1: In a depressed or weak state
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. In a depressed or weak state.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "At a low ebb" means in a poor, weak, or depressed condition or state — a period when something (health, business, morale, etc.) is at its worst. (कमजोर या निराशाजनक स्थिति में)
◦ Example: After losing his job, his confidence was at a low ebb.

• The expression comes from the tide of the sea — "ebb" refers to the outward flow of the tide, and "low ebb" is the point when the tide is at its lowest level, giving rise to the figurative sense of being at one's lowest point.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: In a happy state is incorrect — this is the opposite meaning; "at a low ebb" describes a negative, weakened condition, not happiness.

• Option 3: In a critical moment is incorrect — while a low ebb can be a difficult time, the idiom specifically emphasises weakness/depression, not merely a decisive or critical moment.

• Option 4: In an unemployed mode is incorrect — the idiom is general and can apply to health, finances, morale, business, etc.; it does not specifically mean unemployment.

NOTE

• Other tide-related idioms tested by SSC: "To go with the tide" (to follow the majority or current trend), "To turn the tide" (to reverse the course of events), "The tide has turned" (the situation has changed direction, usually for the better).

question:
Identify the error in the following sentence.
Ourselves should not boast of one's knowledge.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Ourselves.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rule — Reflexive Pronouns: Reflexive pronouns (myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves) cannot be used as the subject of a sentence. They are used only to refer back to a noun/pronoun already mentioned as the subject, either reflexively (the subject acting on itself) or emphatically.

• In the given sentence, "Ourselves" is wrongly used as the subject. It should be replaced with the subject pronoun "We", giving the correct sentence: "We should not boast of one's knowledge."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "one's" is correct; it is properly used here as a possessive form referring to a general/indefinite subject.

• Option 2: "boast" is correct; it is properly used as the main verb of the sentence, correctly following the modal "should not".

• Option 4: "knowledge" is correct; it is properly used as the object of the preposition "of".

NOTE

• Reflexive pronouns can, however, be used as the object of a sentence when the subject and object refer to the same person/thing (e.g., "He hurt himself"), or emphatically right after the subject (e.g., "He himself said so").

• Common SSC trap: sentences beginning with a reflexive pronoun as subject, such as "Myself will do it" (incorrect) instead of "I myself will do it" or simply "I will do it".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
This book giving us much information about our freedom fighters who lost their lives while serving our motherland.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. gives us much information.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "This book", which is third person singular; the verb must therefore be in its singular present-tense form, "gives", not the participle "giving" (which leaves the sentence without a proper finite verb) and not "give" (which is the plural/base form).

• Rule — Countable vs Uncountable Nouns: "Information" is an uncountable noun and is always used with "much", never with "many" (which is reserved for countable plural nouns).

• Combining both corrections gives: "This book gives us much information about our freedom fighters...", which is grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "gives us many information" is incorrect because "information" being uncountable cannot take "many"; it must take "much".

• Option 2: "give us many information" is incorrect on two counts — the verb "give" does not agree with the singular subject "This book", and "many" is wrongly used with the uncountable noun "information".

• Option 3: "give us much information" is incorrect because the verb "give" does not agree with the singular subject "This book"; it should be "gives".

NOTE

• Other common uncountable nouns that take "much"/"little" (not "many"/"few") and are frequently tested: advice, furniture, luggage, news, knowledge, equipment.

• Countable nouns take "many"/"few" (e.g., many books, few chairs).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Off and on
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Now and then.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Off and on" means occasionally, from time to time, at irregular intervals; not continuously. (कभी-कभी / रुक-रुक कर)
◦ Example: It has been raining off and on all day.

• "Now and then" conveys the same sense of intermittent occurrence, making it the correct match.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Know something thoroughly is incorrect — this meaning corresponds to an idiom like "know something inside out" or "at one's fingertips", not "off and on".

• Option 3: Remind is incorrect — "off and on" does not carry the sense of prompting someone to remember something.

• Option 4: Object to is incorrect — this meaning corresponds to idioms like "to take exception to" or "to have a bone to pick with", not "off and on".

NOTE

• Other idioms of frequency/regularity tested by SSC: "Once in a blue moon" (very rarely), "Day in and day out" (continuously, every day), "At regular intervals", and "Every now and again" (occasionally, synonymous with "off and on").

question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence.
A. These are responsible for producing the major fuel used across the globe.
B. The country has 100 major oil and gas fields.
C. The economy of Saudi Arabia is based on petroleum.
D. The chief oil field is Ghawar Field having an estimated 70 billion reserve resource.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. CBAD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage must open with the sentence that introduces the main topic: "The economy of Saudi Arabia is based on petroleum" (C) — this names the subject (Saudi Arabia) and the theme (petroleum-based economy) for the first time.

• This is logically followed by "The country has 100 major oil and gas fields" (B), which elaborates on C by describing the source of this petroleum-based economy — the oil and gas fields.

• Next comes "These are responsible for producing the major fuel used across the globe" (A), where "These" clearly refers back to the "100 major oil and gas fields" mentioned in B, explaining their global significance.

• Finally, "The chief oil field is Ghawar Field having an estimated 70 billion reserve resource" (D) narrows the focus from the general fields to the specific, most important one, forming a logical conclusion.

• Reading the full passage in order C-B-A-D flows coherently from general (Saudi Arabia's economy) to specific (the chief oil field, Ghawar).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. CBAD.

Additional Information

• Option 1: DCAB is incorrect because it starts with a highly specific detail (the Ghawar Field) before the general topic (Saudi Arabia's petroleum-based economy) has even been introduced.

• Option 2: ABCD is incorrect because it starts with "These", a pronoun that has no antecedent at the beginning of the passage.

• Option 4: BACD is incorrect because it begins with "The country", without first identifying which country (Saudi Arabia) is being discussed — that identification only happens in C.

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, always locate the sentence that introduces the subject/topic by name (here, "Saudi Arabia") as a strong candidate for the opening sentence, and track pronouns like "These", "It", "This" to find the sentence they logically refer back to.

question:
Select the option that contains all the MISSPELT words in the following sentences.
1. The new restraunt offers a wide variety of delicious dishes.
2. I can't beleive he made such a silly mistake in his presentation.
3. The teacher asked the students to complete the assigment by Friday.
4. She felt utterly embarassed by her colleague's comments.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. restraunt, beleive, assigment, embarassed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence 1 contains the misspelling "restraunt" — the correct spelling is "restaurant" (the "au" and "ra" are transposed).

• Sentence 2 contains the misspelling "beleive" — the correct spelling is "believe" (violates the "i before e except after c" pattern).

• Sentence 3 contains the misspelling "assigment" — the correct spelling is "assignment" (a silent "n" is missing before "ment").

• Sentence 4 contains the misspelling "embarassed" — the correct spelling is "embarrassed" (it needs a double "r" and a double "s").

• All the other words in the four sentences — "delicious", "wide", "variety", "dishes", "silly", "mistake", "presentation", "teacher", "students", "complete", "Friday", "utterly", "colleague", "comments" — are correctly spelt.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "delicious, beleive, assigment, utterly" is incorrect because "delicious" and "utterly" are both spelt correctly; only "beleive" and "assigment" are actual misspellings here.

• Option 2: "restraunt, silly, assigment, colleague" is incorrect because "silly" and "colleague" are both spelt correctly; the sentence 4 misspelling is actually "embarassed", which this option omits.

• Option 3: "delicious, silly, assigment, colleague" is incorrect because "delicious", "silly" and "colleague" are all spelt correctly; it wrongly excludes "restraunt" and "beleive", and again omits "embarassed".

NOTE

• Memory aids for these commonly misspelt SSC words: Restaurant (rest + au + rant), Believe ("i before e except after c" — b-e-l-i-e-v-e), Assignment (assign + ment, keep the silent "n"), Embarrassed (double "r", double "s" — em-BARR-ASS-ed).

• Other frequently confused spellings tested by SSC: accommodation, occurrence, definitely, separate, necessary, rhythm, questionnaire.

question:
Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank.
My mother said that every relationship must have some amount of ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. flexibility.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "flexibility" — the quality of being able to adapt or change easily, or the ability to bend without breaking.

• Spelling key: FLEX + IBIL + ITY. Note the base word "flex" (not "phlex" or "flax"), followed by "-ibility" (not "-ebelity" or "-ibilety").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "phlexibility" is incorrect — the initial sound is wrongly spelt "ph" instead of "f".

• Option 2: "flexebelity" is incorrect — the middle vowels are wrong; it should be "-ibility", not "-ebelity".

• Option 4: "flaxibilety" is incorrect — the base is wrongly spelt "flax" instead of "flex", and the ending is wrongly spelt "-ilety" instead of "-ility".

NOTE

• The related adjective is "flexible" and the antonym is "rigidity"/"inflexibility".

• Other "-ibility"/"-ability" ending words commonly tested by SSC: responsibility, capability, availability, credibility, possibility — remember these endings are always spelt "-ility", not "-elity" or "-ilety".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
The food intolerance industry has grown dramatically in the previous decade, chiefly because of a boost in Coeliac and Crohn's disease cases, as well as increasing awareness among health-conscious clients.
option_2: pretty much entirely because of a boil-down
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. owing primarily to a rise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined phrase "chiefly because of a boost" means mainly/primarily on account of an increase. The correct substitute must preserve this exact meaning while sounding natural in formal written English.

• "Owing primarily to a rise" matches this meaning precisely: "owing to" = because of, "primarily" = chiefly/mainly, and "a rise" = an increase (in Coeliac and Crohn's disease cases).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "contextually because of a spark" is incorrect — "contextually" (meaning "in a given context") does not convey "chiefly/mainly", and "a spark" suggests a sudden trigger rather than a sustained increase in cases.

• Option 2: "pretty much entirely because of a boil-down" is incorrect — "entirely" overstates "chiefly" (which means mainly, not exclusively), and "a boil-down" (a summary/reduction) does not mean "a boost" (an increase).

• Option 3: "casually due to a growth" is incorrect — "casually" (meaning "in an unplanned, informal manner") wrongly replaces "chiefly" (meaning "mainly"); the two words have entirely different meanings.

NOTE

• In "substitute the underlined segment" questions, the replacement must match both the grammatical role and the precise shade of meaning of the original phrase — near-synonyms that shift the degree of certainty/emphasis (e.g., "entirely" vs "chiefly", "casually" vs "chiefly") are common wrong-option traps.

• Useful synonym set for "chiefly": mainly, primarily, principally, largely, mostly.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
The teenager delivered the speech.
option_1: The speech has been delivered by the teenager.
option_2: The speech is delivered by the teenager.
option_3: The speech was delivered by the teenager.
option_4: The speech was being delivered by the teenager.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The speech was delivered by the teenager.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "The teenager delivered the speech" is an assertive sentence in the Simple Past Tense.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + V2 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "the speech" becomes the subject; since it is singular, the auxiliary is "was"; the verb "delivered" becomes the past participle "delivered" (V3); and "the teenager" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: The speech was delivered by the teenager.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "has been delivered" is the passive form of the Present Perfect Tense, not the Simple Past Tense.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "is delivered" is the passive form of the Simple Present Tense, not the Simple Past Tense.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "was being delivered" is the passive form of the Past Continuous Tense, not the Simple Past Tense.

NOTE

• Quick identification tip: if the active sentence's verb is in the simple past (V2, e.g., "delivered", "saw", "wrote"), the passive must use "was/were + V3" — never "has/have been" (Present Perfect) or "is/are being" (Present Continuous).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
I have booked an apartment in the new residential colony.
option_1: An apartment have been booked by me in the new residential colony.
option_2: An apartment had been booked by me in the new residential colony.
option_3: An apartment is been booked by me in the new residential colony.
option_4: An apartment has been booked by me in the new residential colony.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. An apartment has been booked by me in the new residential colony.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "I have booked an apartment..." is an assertive sentence in the Present Perfect Tense.

• Rule — Present Perfect Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + has/have + been + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "an apartment" becomes the subject; being singular, it takes the auxiliary "has"; "book" becomes the past participle "booked" (V3); and "I" becomes the agent, "by me".
◦ Passive: An apartment has been booked by me in the new residential colony.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "have been booked" wrongly uses the plural auxiliary "have" with the singular subject "An apartment"; it should be "has been booked".

• Option 2 is incorrect because "had been booked" is the passive form of the Past Perfect Tense, not the Present Perfect Tense used in the original sentence.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "is been booked" is an ungrammatical construction — "is" cannot combine with "been booked"; the correct auxiliary combination for present perfect passive is "has/have been + V3".

NOTE

• In the passive voice, the auxiliary "has/have/had been" must always agree in number with the new subject (the original object), just as in the active voice it must agree with the original subject.

• Present Perfect passive structure to remember firmly: has/have + been + V3.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold.
The city has immense coal piers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. huge.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Immense means extremely large or great in size, extent, or degree. (विशाल / बहुत बड़ा)
◦ Example: The company suffered immense losses after the factory fire.

• Huge carries the same meaning of great size, making it the closest synonym of "immense".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: diminutive (लघु/छोटा): Extremely small in size — this is the opposite meaning of "immense".

• Option 2: trifling (तुच्छ): Of little value or importance; trivial — unrelated to the sense of large size.

• Option 3: set: Fixed or established; has no connection with the meaning of size/magnitude conveyed by "immense".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "immense" frequently tested by SSC: enormous, vast, colossal, gigantic, tremendous.

• Corresponding antonyms to remember: tiny, minute, diminutive, trifling, negligible.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Culture is (1)________, understanding, and protecting, like the cultivation of a garden, not the destruction or eradication of its roots. Understanding the roots and seeds, taking much care and providing instructed nourishment (2)________ important for good gardening. Culture also is similar; understanding its acquaintance (3)________ literature and art and careful protection are required. Culture is the way of life of a particular society in which a group of people live together in one place. The society's culture is visible in its literature, arts, social system, language and religion. It is a combination of traditions, customs, institutions, food habits, manners, morals, thoughts, tastes, views and beliefs. Usually, families (4)________ culture to the younger generations. As family system is becoming weak, schools, colleges and universities should take up this responsibility as education should promote potential values of its culture. The role of universities (5)________ only to issue course completed certificates.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. creating.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "Culture is (1)________, understanding, and protecting, like the cultivation of a garden..." — here, the blank is part of a list of three parallel actions describing what culture involves, joined by "and": "___, understanding, and protecting".

• Rule — Parallelism: When multiple verb forms are joined in a list by "and"/"or", they must all be in the same grammatical form. Since "understanding" and "protecting" are both gerunds (V-ing forms), the first blank must also be a gerund to maintain parallel structure.

• The correct gerund form is "creating", giving: "Culture is creating, understanding, and protecting..." — a grammatically parallel and meaningful list.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "creation" is incorrect because it is a noun, not a gerund/verb form, and does not fit the "is ___, understanding, and protecting" structure grammatically.

• Option 2: "to create" is incorrect because it is an infinitive; mixing an infinitive with two gerunds ("understanding", "protecting") breaks the required parallel structure.

• Option 3: "create" is incorrect because it is the base form of the verb, which cannot follow "is" directly, nor does it match the gerund forms used elsewhere in the list.

NOTE

• The rule of parallelism is one of the most frequently tested grammar concepts in SSC cloze passages: always scan the words on either side of a blank (here, "understanding" and "protecting") to identify the required form before selecting the option.

• Common parallel structures tested: gerund lists (V-ing, V-ing, and V-ing), infinitive lists (to + V1, to + V1, and to + V1) — never mix the two within one list.

The role of universities (5)________ only to issue course completed certificates.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. are.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The relevant part of the sentence reads: "Understanding the roots and seeds, taking much care and providing instructed nourishment (2)________ important for good gardening."

• The subject of the blank is the compound subject formed by three coordinated gerund phrases: "Understanding the roots and seeds", "taking much care", and "providing instructed nourishment". Multiple items joined together in this way form a plural compound subject.

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement: A compound subject made up of more than one item joined by "and" generally takes a plural verb. Since the sentence is in the Simple Present Tense, the plural verb required is "are".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "is" is incorrect because it is a singular present-tense verb, which does not agree with the plural compound subject.

• Option 2: "were" is incorrect because it is a past-tense verb, while the rest of the passage (e.g., "is", "are") is written in the present tense, and it is also grammatically not the standard choice for a compound plural subject in present context.

• Option 3: "was" is incorrect because it is both singular and past tense, matching neither the number (plural subject) nor the tense (present) required here.

NOTE

• When a sentence's subject consists of several gerund phrases or actions joined by "and", treat the subject as plural for the purpose of subject-verb agreement, unless the actions are considered as a single combined idea.

• Always check the surrounding sentences of a cloze passage for the dominant tense being used, to avoid selecting an option that is correct in isolation but breaks the tense consistency of the whole paragraph.

The role of universities (5)________ only to issue course completed certificates.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The relevant part of the sentence reads: "Culture also is similar; understanding its acquaintance (3)________ literature and art and careful protection are required."

• Rule — Fixed Preposition: The noun "acquaintance" is conventionally followed by the preposition "with" when referring to familiarity or knowledge of something — "acquaintance with".

• Applying the rule: "understanding its acquaintance with literature and art" correctly expresses familiarity/knowledge of literature and art.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "for" is incorrect because "acquaintance for" is not a standard or grammatically accepted collocation in English.

• Option 2: "on" is incorrect because "acquaintance on" is not the correct fixed preposition used with this noun.

• Option 4: "in" is incorrect because "acquaintance in" is not idiomatically correct; "with" is the only preposition conventionally paired with "acquaintance" in this sense.

NOTE

• Other nouns/adjectives that are fixed with the preposition "with" and frequently tested by SSC: familiar with, satisfied with, compare with, deal with, sympathy with, consistent with.

• Do not confuse "acquainted with" (adjective + with) with "acquaintance of" (used only when referring to a person one knows, e.g., "He is an acquaintance of mine").

The role of universities (5)________ only to issue course completed certificates.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. transmit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The relevant part of the sentence reads: "Usually, families (4)________ culture to the younger generations."

• The subject of the blank is "families", which is a plural noun. The sentence is in the Simple Present Tense, as indicated by the adverb "Usually", which signals a habitual/general action.

• Rule — Simple Present Tense: With a plural subject, the main verb takes its base form (V1), without the "-s"/"-es" ending. Since "families" is plural, the correct verb form is "transmit".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "transmitting" is incorrect because a bare gerund/present participle cannot function as the main finite verb of the sentence without an auxiliary like "are".

• Option 2: "transmitted" is incorrect because it is the past tense/past participle form, which does not match the Simple Present Tense established by "Usually" and the rest of the passage.

• Option 4: "transmits" is incorrect because "-s" is added only for a singular (third person) subject; "families" is plural, so the base form "transmit" is needed, not "transmits".

NOTE

• Adverbs of frequency/habit such as "usually", "always", "often", "generally" are strong signal words indicating the Simple Present Tense in cloze passages.

• Subject-verb agreement rule to remember: singular subject + verb-with-"s"/"es" (transmits); plural subject + base verb (transmit).

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Culture is (1)________, understanding, and protecting, like the cultivation of a garden, not the destruction or eradication of its roots. Understanding the roots and seeds, taking much care and providing instructed nourishment (2)________ important for good gardening. Culture also is similar; understanding its acquaintance (3)________ literature and art and careful protection are required. Culture is the way of life of a particular society in which a group of people live together in one place. The society's culture is visible in its literature, arts, social system, language and religion. It is a combination of traditions, customs, institutions, food habits, manners, morals, thoughts, tastes, views and beliefs. Usually, families (4)________ culture to the younger generations. As family system is becoming weak, schools, colleges and universities should take up this responsibility as education should promote potential values of its culture. The role of universities (5)________ only to issue course completed certificates.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. should not be restricted.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The relevant part of the sentence reads: "The role of universities (5)________ only to issue course completed certificates."

• The overall argument of the passage is that, as the family system weakens, schools, colleges and universities should take up the responsibility of passing on culture, and that education should promote the values of culture — meaning universities' role should be broader than merely issuing certificates.

• The word "only" immediately after the blank signals a restrictive/limiting idea; the sense required is that the role of universities should NOT be limited to just issuing certificates. This requires the negative passive modal structure "should not be restricted".

• Rule — Modal + Passive Voice: The structure modal + be + V3 (e.g., "should be restricted") is used to form the passive of a modal verb; adding "not" after the modal negates it, giving "should not be restricted".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "should be restricted" is incorrect because it reverses the intended meaning — the passage argues that universities' role should expand beyond certification, not be limited to it.

• Option 2: "restrict" is incorrect because it is an active-voice base verb with no modal or subject-agreement structure; it cannot grammatically follow "The role of universities" directly.

• Option 3: "should restricted" is incorrect because it is grammatically malformed — a modal verb like "should" must be followed by the base form of "be" (i.e., "should be restricted"), not directly by the past participle "restricted".

NOTE

• Modal passive structure to remember: modal + be + V3 (e.g., should be done, must be completed, can be achieved); its negative form is modal + not + be + V3.

• In cloze passages, always read beyond the sentence containing the blank — the overall tone/argument of the passage (here, that universities should take on a bigger cultural role) is often essential to choosing the semantically correct option.
